title: Audit accessibility across the signed-in Zedu workspace
description: Review keyboard-only and screen-reader access in the authenticated product for the principal organizer and learner workflows. Use a designated test workspace and synthetic records only. Deliver a reproducible issue log with affected steps, assistive technology, impact, applicable WCAG 2.2 guidance, prioritized fixes and a retest plan. Do not access real learner data or publish an accessibility claim before verification.

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Audit six fixed organizer and learner journeys against WCAG 2.2, starting with the criteria most audits skip
acceptedWorkstreams.description:
Verified first (zeduchat/zedu-fe, main, 22 Oct 2026 - leads, not findings, until confirmed on screen):
- No skip-to-content link anywhere in src/.
- tabIndex appears twice in the app, while 10 <div>/<span> carry an onClick with no role and no tabIndex (e.g. menu-dropdown/index.tsx:66). The app is built on Radix, so primitives are fine; the keyboard path breaks where app code replaces a Radix part with a clickable div.
- No automated a11y tooling: no axe, no eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y, though the repo has 15 Cypress specs. Nothing catches a regression.
- No accessibility statement page yet, which is correct given the goal's ban on publishing one before verification.

Approach:
1. Matrix first: six journeys - organizer: create workspace, invite member, set role, start Buzz call, upload file; learner: accept invite, open thread, submit assignment - each with numbered steps, the AT (NVDA+Firefox, VoiceOver+Safari) and a synthetic workspace with fake records only. Every finding cites a matrix ID.
2. Test the WCAG 2.2 criteria audits skip: 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured, 2.5.7 Dragging Movements, 2.5.8 Target Size, 3.3.7 Redundant Entry, 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication. New in 2.2, never tested against.
3. Code gives leads, the screen confirms them: the 10 clickable divs, 8 dangerouslySetInnerHTML (ChannelMessage/formatMessage.tsx), the missing skip link. Each confirmed or dropped with screen, AT and step number, so no code-reading guesses enter it.
4. Make it re-runnable: add an axe-core spec to the existing Cypress suite for machine-checkable failures; keep the manual screen-reader pass for the rest.

Done: issue log (journey ID, step, AT+browser, criterion, impact, screen, zedu-fe file); prioritised fix list tied to files; retest plan; the Cypress spec as a diff, not deployed. No statement before the retest, no real learner data.

Measured by: how many of the six journeys a keyboard-only user completes end to end, issues closed and re-verified, axe violations in CI at zero.

upvotes.reason: "Audit six fixed organizer and learner journeys against WCAG 2.2, starting with the criteria most audits skip" gives the team evidence it can act on, with every claim carrying its source, so the result holds up when someone checks it. it produces something checkable rather than an opinion, so the goal either moved or it did not.

This approach matches the authenticated accessibility goal by requiring synthetic records, numbered journey steps, actual keyboard/screen-reader evidence and a manual retest alongside automation. I support its explicit distinction between code leads and confirmed findings; axe alone cannot establish conformance. Before assigning work, reconcile the six-journey title with the eight listed actions and confirm which AT/browser combinations the worker can actually test. Missing access must remain a blocker, not a claimed pass.
Critical accessibility and technical foundation: auditing live organizer journeys against WCAG 2.2 ensures compliance for institutional and educational buyers.

Anchoring 'Audit accessibility across the signed-in Zedu workspace' in verified operational workflows and empirical research accelerates adoption while preventing wasted feature churn.

pendingIdeas.title: Add axe-core checks to zedu-fe's existing Cypress suite, so the audited journeys don't regress after fixes
pendingIdeas.description: zedu-fe already has a Cypress suite (cypress.config.ts and e2e specs for auth and Buzz). Approach: add cypress-axe to the journeys the audit covers, run it against the test workspace, and fail on new serious or critical violations while recording existing ones as a baseline. This complements the manual audit, which catches what automated rules can't (reading order, meaningful labels, focus after actions). Done: the proposed spec changes, the first baseline report, and the rule for when a new violation blocks a release.

upvotes.reason: For this goal specifically, "Add axe-core checks to zedu-fe's existing Cypress suite, so the audited journeys don't regress after fixes" reaches people who are not yet searching for Zedu by name, and it ends in something an editor can check rather than a post. it fills a gap the goal has open rather than restating what is already covered.
